question: Measured over a fixed 20-item sample, how many distinct, non-duplicate mechanisms does a video/talk transcript produce per 10k tokens of extraction cost, compared with the blog-post and official-docs classes over the same subject matter - and does it clear the threshold to stay in the default source-class set?

reviewer.method: Second named probe rebuilds planted restatements from blog bytes (not by trusting the stored talk) and requires unique_after_collapse==0. A mutant that treats restatements as unique is rejected.

tests.covers: two restatement talks collapse against companion blogs

threshold.rule: Transcript class stays in the default source-class set iff incremental unique-mechanism yield per 10k tokens, after collapsing restatement transcripts against companion blogs, is >= 1.0 AND >= 0.50 times the official-docs class incremental yield per 10k tokens.

tokenizer.peer_algorithm: identical regex unigram; distinct pin name for this unit
tokenizer.spec: Unicode regex unigram: '(?:[sdmt]|ll|ve|re)| ?[^\W\d_]+| ?\d+| ?[^\s\w]+|\s+(?!\S)|\s+ with unmatched gaps kept as their own tokens. Each piece counts as 1. Not len(text)//4.

two_signal.signal_a: tokenizer unigram token count of extracted plaintext per item (not chars/4)
two_signal.signal_b: UTF-8 byte length of capture bytes (CRLF-normalised) plus Jaccard-clustered mechanism fingerprints
